title: Building Agents with Amazon Nova Act and MCP - Du'An Lightfoot, Amazon (Full Workshop)
talk_summary: A hands-on AWS workshop demoing Amazon Nova Act (browser-automation model), wrapping it in an MCP server, and wiring it into Strands agents with MCP-native tool support. Most content is live demo and Q&A about browser automation limits; the transferable parts are MCP server design discipline and thin agent frameworks.

takeaways.technique: MCP server as portable capability layer
takeaways.what_they_do: They wrap a capability (Nova Act browser actions) in an MCP server exposing discrete tools (browse session, browser action, execute parallel task, screenshots, close browser, list results), then plug the same server into different clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Amazon Q CLI) without rewriting code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So that's the beauty of MCP. I already have this server. I can just use a different client.

takeaways.technique: Prescriptive tool descriptions in the server
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the hardest part of an MCP server is encoding when/how to use each tool and its inputs/outputs, and they bake prescriptive action phrasing into the server so clients make good calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Probably one of the hardest things about making the MCP servers that's making sure you provide a next context of when to use the tool, how to use the tool, the inputs and outputs.

takeaways.technique: Thin model-first agent framework with agents-as-tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Strands defines an agent as just prompt + model + tools; a Python function with a tool decorator becomes a tool, and sub-agents are passed as tools to an orchestrator that decides sequencing itself rather than a hardcoded flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't specifically say do this one first, do that first. We'll let the the agent figure that out.
takeaways.numbers: multi-agent solution in under 50 lines of code; ~40 lines for two MCP servers + agent

takeaways.what_they_do: The same agent code runs on Bedrock, LiteLLM, or Ollama by changing the model reference, so the framework does not lock you to one provider.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use another model with light LLM. Yep. So, you don't need AWS at all in that instance.

takeaways.technique: Browser automation for UI smoke tests
takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest Nova Act can drive a browser in natural language for UI testing, replacing brittle selector-based Selenium/Playwright scripts, with headless parallel execution of independent tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can just write in natural language you know click this button click that button so yes it can handle that use case

takeaways.technique: Headless/parallel browser execution in isolated VMs
takeaways.what_they_do: They run browser agents headless via Xvfb framebuffer in a cloud VM, and launch multiple independent tasks as parallel threads to avoid serial waiting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's running F XVFB. It's a frame buffer where it runs your X11 system.
